note: The 2004 edition reduces the eulogy to the sole Theogenes

The historical editions commemorate a bishop Euphrasius in Africa on this day; the 2004 edition's eulogy of the day is Euphrasius, bishop of Clermont (mr:0114-euphrasius). The two are keyed apart and linked as the same eulogy, whose subject the 2004 edition changed.
The 1914 English fuses the eulogies of Ingenuinus and Albuinus of Brixen, which the 1749 edition and the 2004 edition print separately (mr:0205-ingenuinus, mr:0205-albuinus); it is linked to both.

The 1749 edition names Eleutherius, bishop, and 128 others in Persia on February 20; probably the eulogy of Sadoth, bishop, and 128 companions (mr:0218-sadoth-et-socii): same place, king (Sapor), number and refusal to adore the sun (#47).

The 1749 and 1914 editions print the thirty-nine martyrs of the mines of Phaeno as a eulogy of their own, after that of Silvanus of Gaza; the 2004 edition commemorates them together with him in mr:0504-silvanus-et-socii.
The 2004 edition reduces the eulogy to Quintus alone (mr:0905-v, see #52).
The 2004 edition drops Mark and leads with the three brothers.
The historical editions place Maximus at Apamea, 2004 at Cumae: keyed apart and matched, as Euphrasius on 0114.
